Assumptions / Conditions / Definitions.
- Let $\operatorname{Sym}(V \otimes E)$, $R_n^{(m)}$, and $I$ be as in Proposition 1.

The $GL(E)$ character of $R_n^{(m)}$ decomposes identically as $\sum_\lambda c_\lambda(n) s_\lambda(E)$. The coefficients $c_\lambda(n)$ are universal non-negative integers that do not depend on $m$ (provided $m \ge \ell(\lambda)$).
fixed_proof: By Cauchy's formula, $\operatorname{Sym}(V \otimes E)$ decomposes as a $GL(V) \times GL(E)$ module into $\bigoplus_{\lambda} S^\lambda(V) \otimes S^\lambda(E)$. Because the quotient ideal $I$ is $S_n$-invariant, the $GL(E)$ character of $R_n^{(m)}$ decomposes identically as $\sum_\lambda c_\lambda(n) s_\lambda(E)$.
